PullRequest.Title: test: fix resolver tunnel port allocation and bind errors
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary
Narrowed to the test resolver only. The browser-tools HTTP fixture is handled independently by #336988; this PR no longer changes that test.

- When the requested local port equals the remote port (the test resolver runs both on the same machine), let the OS allocate a free local port instead of assuming `remotePort + 1` is available. The adjacent port can be occupied or reserved on Windows, and remote port 65535 would otherwise produce an invalid local port.
- Reject tunnel creation on a server bind error instead of leaving the promise pending.
- Preserve explicitly requested distinct local ports and existing privileged-port behavior.

This addresses the resolver failure behind the rollback in #336381. It is not an additional failure established in Azure build 475409, and #336988 does not require this change because it uses the browser remote proxy without explicitly opening a tunnel.

## Validation
- After narrowing: both test extensions compile with zero errors; scoped hygiene (including ESLint) and `git diff --check` pass.
- Direct compiled-resolver probes passed: remote port 65535 allocates a valid local port; an occupied explicitly requested local port rejects with `EADDRINUSE`.
- The resolver implementation is unchanged from `ec5a082570d`, validated by [Azure build 475477](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=475477): **succeeded**, with all Electron and Remote integration jobs passing on Windows x64, Linux x64, and macOS ARM64. That revision still included the now-removed HTTP fixture, which explicitly exercised tunnel creation in remote tests.
- The scope-only follow-up commit has not been rerun in Azure.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: An ignored server bind error leaves the tunnel provider promise and per-port in-progress state pending indefinitely.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: A test-resolver tunnel request hangs indefinitely when its local port cannot be bound.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: A server bind failure now rejects tunnel creation, allowing the open-tunnel critical path and factory-in-progress cleanup to complete instead of waiting indefinitely.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The base implementation creates the tunnel promise with an unused rejection callback and listens without a server error handler. A bind failure therefore leaves the provider promise pending. ExtHostTunnelService awaits the provider, and AbstractTunnelService stores that promise and retains its factory-in-progress key until settlement, so tunnel opening cannot complete. The changed line forwards the pre-listen server error to the promise rejection callback.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a new test-resolver tunnel when the preferred local port equals the remote port
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The workbench sends one tunnel-provider IPC request, the extension host invokes tunnelFactory, and tunnel opening waits for net.Server.listen to bind before returning the selected local address. This bind is on the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the remote authority resolver tunnel factory in the extension host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per cold unique remote host/port; warm requests reuse the tunnel service entry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider IPC call occurred on cold tunnel creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The response must return before tunnel opening completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Bind a loopback TCP server for the local tunnel endpoint.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bind per cold tunnel creation, after host/port coalescing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One bind was also performed, using remotePort + 1 when the preferred local and remote ports matched; the diff instead requests one OS-assigned free port.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The listen callback must run before the tunnel is returned.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of distinct remote endpoints opened in the test session; repeated requests for one endpoint are coalesced/cached.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: AbstractTunnelService caches successful tunnels by remote host/port and prevents a second factory invocation for the same remote port while creation is in progress. Different remote ports may be created concurrently, unchanged by this diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold creation performs one IPC and one bind. Successful tunnels are cached by remote host/port and refcounted; warm opens reuse the promise/tunnel without another bind. There is no separate negative cache introduced by the port-selection change.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the diff, provider call chain, bind, and tunnel map behavior are directly visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Kernel ephemeral-port selection cost is platform-dependent, but it replaces rather than adds a bind and is normally constant-time relative to this test workflow.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff changes the requested bind port from an adjacent fixed port to port 0 without increasing boundary-call count, serialized work, allocation, or retained state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a tunnel with an explicitly requested distinct local port, including a bind conflict
Scenarios.CriticalPath: One provider IPC and one loopback server bind must settle before the tunnel request can complete. On bind failure, the added listener now rejects that critical-path promise instead of leaving it pending.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Await the resolver's tunnelFactory result across the main-thread/extension-host boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call for a cold remote endpoint; same-endpoint attempts during creation are suppressed and successful endpoints are cached.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same IPC was issued, but a bind error left its provider promise unresolved.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Tunnel opening waits for the provider result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Attempt to bind the explicitly requested loopback port.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bind attempt per cold endpoint; no retry loop or fan-out is added.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same bind was attempted, but its error was not connected to the tunnel promise, causing an indefinite wait.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Success returns the tunnel; failure now rejects immediately through the added one-shot listener.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct tunnel endpoints whose requested local ports are unavailable; realistic test runs generally open only a small number.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One factory call is active per remote port; distinct remote ports may proceed concurrently. The finally handler clears the in-progress key once the newly rejected promise settles.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Successful tunnels remain cached/refcounted. A failed bind now settles and releases the factory-in-progress key. The tunnel map's handling of provider rejection is outside this diff; compared with the previous pending promise, the change does not add retained entries or retries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: Node server error semantics and the awaited provider path directly establish the before/after behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Bind-conflict prevalence varies by platform and test environment, but the prior indefinite wait and the changed rejection mechanism are certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced performance issue. This is a latency/cleanup improvement; the concrete indefinite-wait regression fix was recorded separately.

Scenarios.Scenario: Proxy traffic through an established test-resolver tunnel
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After listen succeeds, each accepted local TCP connection opens one remote TCP connection; that connect is on the data path for that client connection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open one TCP connection to the remote address and pipe bytes bidirectionally.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One remote connection per accepted local client connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical per-connection connect and piping behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for that client's proxied traffic, but not for initial tunnel creation because it runs only after a client connects.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of simultaneous or sequential client connections through the established tunnel.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Connections are handled independently by Node's server; no new limiter, queue, or concurrency burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The established server/tunnel is reused for its endpoint until disposal; this diff does not change connection caching or tunnel disposal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the connection callback is unchanged and remains downstream of the modified bind setup.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Traffic volume is test-dependent, but the diff does not alter its cardinality or per-connection work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression because runtime proxy traffic work, concurrency, and network-call count are unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete one-file diff and traced tunnel creation, caching/coalescing, IPC, TCP bind, error, disposal, and traffic paths. No diff-introduced performance regression was found. The PR changes one bind-port choice without adding work and fixes an existing indefinite tunnel-creation wait on bind errors; that regression fix was recorded with its blamed introducing commit.
